{{Use mdy dates|date=January 2015}} {{Infobox Election | election_name = United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa, 2018 | country = Iowa | type = legislative | ongoing = yes | previous_election = United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa, 2016 | previous_year = 2016 | next_election = United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa, 2020 | next_year = 2020 | seats_for_election = All 4 Iowa seats to the [[United States House of Representatives]] | election_date = {{Start date|2018|11|06}} | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | last_election1 = 3 | seats1 = | seat_change1 = | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | swing1 = | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | last_election2 = 1 | seats2 = | seat_change2 = | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | swing2 = | map_image = | map_caption = }} {{ElectionsIA}} The '''2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa''' will be held on November 6, 2018, to elect the four [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Iowa]], one from each of the state's four [[Iowa's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with the [[Iowa gubernatorial election, 2018|gubernatorial election]], as well as [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2018|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[United States Senate elections, 2018|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[United States elections, 2018|state and local elections]]. {{Toclimit|limit=2}} ==District 1== {{see also|Iowa's 1st congressional district}} [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Rod Blum]], who has represented the district since 2015, was reelected to a second term with 54% of the vote in 2016. The 1st district went for Donald Trump in the 2016 presidential election with a 49% to 45% margin, after voting for Barack Obama with a 56% to 43% margin in 2012.{{cite web|url=http://www.dailykos.com/story/2016/12/06/1607696/-Morning-Digest-Facing-reality-Pat-McCrory-finally-concedes-North-Carolina-governor-s-race|title=Morning Digest: Facing reality, Pat McCrory finally concedes North Carolina governor's race|work=[[Daily Kos|Daily Kos Elections]]|date=December 6, 2016|accessdate=January 18, 2017}} ===Democratic primary=== ====Candidates==== ;Declared * [[Abby Finkenauer]], Iowa State Representative{{cite web|url=http://iowastartingline.com/2017/05/03/abby-finkenauer-launches-congressional-bid-working-class-message/ |title=ABBY FINKENAUER LAUNCHES CONGRESSIONAL BID ON WORKING CLASS MESSAGE |publisher=Iowa Starting Line |author=Pat Rynard |date=May 3, 2017 |accessdate=May 3, 2017}} * Thomas Heckroth, former staffer for United States Senator [[Tom Harkin]]{{cite web|url=http://globegazette.com/news/iowa/thomas-heckroth-joins-field-of-candidates-seeking-to-unseat-u/article_ea280f9e-839d-5b47-abd0-3618b3d9f5ae.html |title=Thomas Heckroth joins field of candidates seeking to unseat U.S. Rep.
